messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Turkish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Turkish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------| | ove | locative adverb “where” introducing a place clause | **orada** | “there / where” | OK | | udirai | future 2nd sg “you will hear” | **duyacaksın** | “you will hear” | OK | | le | definite article, fem. pl “the” (object) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Turkish has no article) | | disperate | adjective “despairing, desperate” | **umutsuz** | “desperate” | OK | | strida | noun fem. pl “shrieks” | **çığlıkları** | “the shrieks” | OK | | vedrai | future 2nd sg “you will see” | **göreceksin** | “you will see” | OK | | li | definite article, masc. pl “the” (object) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | antichi | adjective “ancient” | **eski** | “ancient” | OK | | spiriti | noun masc. pl “spirits” | **ruhları** | “the spirits” | OK | | dolenti | adjective “woeful, sorrowful” | **acı çeken** | “suffering / woeful” | OK | | ch' | relative pronoun “who/that” introducing a clause | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | a | preposition “to / toward” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | la | definite article, fem. sg “the” (object) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | seconda | ordinal adjective “second” | **ikinci** | “second” | OK | | morte | noun fem. sg “death” (object of *a*) | **ölümü** | “death” | OK | | ciascun | distributive pronoun “each” | **her biri** | “each one” | OK | | grida | verb 3rd sg present “shouts / cries out” | **haykırıyor** | “shouts” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: le, li, la, ch', a – Turkish naturally omits these articles and the relative/prepositional markers without loss of meaning. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Turkish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Turkish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 115** - Original: *orada umutsuz çığlıkları duyacaksın,* - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 116** - Original: *eski acı çeken ruhları göreceksin,* - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 117** - Original: *her biri ikinci ölümü haykırıyor;* - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
